name: ICRTAC'26 - 9th Intl Conf on Recent Trends in Advanced Computing (VIT Chennai, SCOPE)
publisher_indexing: 2026 site: accepted, registered and presented papers are 'submitted for inclusion in IEEE Xplore' subject to IEEE scope and quality review (call says in association with IEEE Madras Section, conf #70537). Springer CCIS is NOT mentioned on the 2026 site. Springer did publish the 2024 edition (CCIS vol. 2608, 36 full papers from 315 submissions); the 2023 edition was IEEE. Scopus: not verified.
scope: General advanced computing; 2026 theme is sustainability/SDGs; topic list includes blockchain and secure systems, cybersecurity and privacy.
format: IEEE double column, max 6 pages including references, 250-word abstract; Microsoft CMT.
deadline: ICRTAC'26 closed: paper deadline 15 Aug 2026 (site: 'submissions closed'); notification 17 Oct 2026; registration 1 Nov 2026; camera-ready 5 Nov 2026; conference 10-11 Dec 2026. 2027 edition: not verified.
cost: Registration (Indian authors, non-IEEE/IEEE member): UG/PG student INR 7,500/7,000; research scholar 8,000/7,500; faculty 8,500/8,000; industry 9,500. Foreign USD 300. Non-refundable.
fit_reason: Scope and 6-page IEEE length suit the paper and it is hosted by the authors' own university, but this cycle is closed so it only helps if a 2027 edition appears.
red_flags: Publisher changed between editions (IEEE 2023, Springer 2024, IEEE Xplore 'submission' 2026), so do not assume Springer. 2024 acceptance was about 11% (36/315), which contradicts 'easy to accept'. Mandatory registration fee for each accepted paper.

name: E-Vote-ID - Intl Joint Conference on Electronic Voting
publisher_indexing: 2025 CFP: Springer LNCS (selection of full papers, tracks 1-2) and GI Lecture Notes in Informatics (selection of full and short papers, tracks 1-3); all papers open access. 2025 LNCS vol. 16028: 13 full papers from 39 submissions. 2026 proceedings page links a Springer volume (DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-39512-2). Scopus: not verified.
scope: Voting technology, governance, practical election experiences, posters/demos, PhD colloquium; double-blind, EasyChair.
format: 2025 CFP (LNCS format): full 16 pages; work-in-progress/SoK 20 pages (4-page summary after acceptance); short papers 4 pages; Track 4 posters/demonstrations take a short abstract.
deadline: 2026 edition was 6-9 Oct 2026 in Tallinn (already held). 2027 CFP not found: not verified. For reference, 2025 deadlines were 15 May (tracks 1-2), 10 Jul (track 3 and PhD), 15 Sep (posters/demos); do not assume 2027 matches.
fit_reason: Best topical home: Track 3 (election and practical experiences), short paper or Track 4 demo accept implemented systems, though Track 1 reviewers will expect stronger security analysis and the paper is explicitly not end-to-end verifiable.
red_flags: None seen; reviewers are voting-security specialists, so expect critical review of the threat model. Travel to Europe is costly.

name: Voting'27 - 12th Workshop on Advances in Secure Electronic Voting (with Financial Cryptography 2027, Barbados)
publisher_indexing: Voting'26 proceedings: Springer LNCS (per FC26 CFP page). Voting'27 page says 'Workshop information coming soon'. Scopus: not verified.
scope: Secure e-voting; E2E-verifiable schemes, attacks, implementations, deployment experience with rigorous analysis.
format: Voting'26 rules (may change): LNCS, double-blind; full 15 pages; short papers 8 pages (title starts 'Short paper') for work in progress and novel applications or voting experiences.

red_flags: Costly Caribbean travel; one author must attend. Dual-submission rules mean wait for the CFP before committing.
